title: Accessible (?) Data “Visualisation”
text:
Accessibility
Over a billion people (more than 15% of the global population) have at least one disability (WHO 2022).
The 2019 European Accessibility Act (EEA) just came into effect in June 2025 and requires EU products to be accessible.
The Web Content Accessibility Guidelines (WCAG) published by the World Wide Web Consortium (3WC) promote content to be:

perceivable to multiple senses (e.g., alt text)
operable in multiple modes (e.g., keyboard navigation)
understandable through a simple and intuitive interface
robust with current and future tech (e.g, reading machine)

title: Accessible (?) Data “Visualisation”
text:
Multi-sensory visualisation
For more accessible data visualisation, we can leverage multiple sensory modalities.

“Data visualisation implies vision, but vision is not always available, or complexity might be visually overwhelming.”
— Markku Häkkinen


“We shouldn’t abbreviate the truth but rather get a new method of presentation.”
― Edward Tufte

Learn how to land a plane, then check out theme_tufte().

title: Accessible (?) Data “Visualisation”
text:
Alt text
Alt text should not be a copy of the figure caption, as it serves a different purpose (accessibility vs context/emphasis).
Alt text should be a clear and complete description of visual content (e.g, a figure), going from general to narrow focus, from major to minor aspects.

Example of alt text from my master thesis

Tactile paper
Paper with embossed Braille text and graphics. A special (expensive) paper and machine are required, but printing is easy and fast (seconds to minutes).

Haptics
Vibration, pressure, ultrasound, electric stimulation, or anything that can mimic the experience of touch.
Create haptic feedback on W3C Vibration API or HTML.

title: Accessible (?) Data “Visualisation”
text:
R toolkit 4 Ally
How can I make my tables and figures more accessible?

Data textualisation (BrailleR)
Data sonification (sonify)
Data tactualisation (tactileR)
Every ggplotter’s broken dream (playitbyr) 🤩😭


# iris dataset vars mapped to pitch, time, modulation freq and index
sonify(iris, sonaes(time = Petal.Length, pitch = Petal.Width,
                    mod = Sepal.Length, indx = Sepal.Width)) +
  shape_scatter() +
  scale_time_continuous(c(0, 10)) +
  scale_pitch_continuous(c(7, 12))
